title: Give the model knowledge it was never trained on
brief: The model must answer from information it was never trained on. You can paste it into the prompt, retrieve it per question, preload and cache it, or train it in. Decide with the corpus size, the change rate and the permission model on the table.

blocks.text: What the evidence says about long inputs

items.label: Context Rot (Chroma, 2025-07-14)
items.note: Performance grows unreliable as input grows, even on simple tasks [[r22]]

items.label: RULER
items.note: Only about half of those claiming 32K or more stayed satisfactory at 32K [[r23]]

items.label: NoLiMa
items.note: Models claiming 128K or more fell below 50% of their short-context baseline at 32K. GPT-4o went from 99.3% to 69.7% [[r41]]

items.label: Anthropic rule of thumb
items.note: About 500 pages (an estimate). Below that, the knowledge base can go in the prompt, with prompt caching [[r42]]

items.label: Contextual retrieval
items.note: Fewer failed retrievals, or with reranking [[r42]]

blocks.title: Four ways to give the model knowledge
blocks.intro: The studies used 2024 to 2025 models. A re-run on 2026 models was not found as of 2026-10-13, so test at your own prompt length.

options.name: Long context in the prompt
options.summary: Paste the documents into every request.
cons: Accuracy drops with length and with position: best at the start and end, worst in the middle [[r40]]
Cost and the 272K price step on GPT-6
options.bestWhen: The corpus is small, changes rarely and has one audience.
options.avoidWhen: The corpus is large, permissions differ by user, or accuracy must hold deep in the prompt.

options.name: RAG
options.summary: Retrieve the relevant chunks per question.
options.bestWhen: The corpus is large or fast-changing, ACLs apply or citations are required.
options.avoidWhen: The corpus is tiny and stable, so the machinery buys nothing.

options.name: Cache-augmented generation
options.summary: Preload a small corpus into a long context and cache its state, with no retrieval step [[r24]].
pros: No retrieval latency or retrieval errors
Cheap repeats when the cache hits
cons: A changed corpus invalidates the cache
One shared context cannot be filtered per user
options.bestWhen: A small, stable corpus serves many questions and latency matters.
options.avoidWhen: Content updates often or exceeds the window.

options.name: Fine-tuning
pros: Format, tone, shorter prompts, smaller models and tool-use behaviour [[r48]]
cons: Weak for facts. RAG beat unsupervised fine-tuning [[r43]], and new facts are learned slowly and then raise hallucination [[r44]]
options.bestWhen: You need a style, a format or a cheaper model.
options.avoidWhen: You want to add facts or keep them current.

blocks.title: Prompt, RAG, cache or fine-tune
blocks.prompt: Change the corpus, the change rate, the access model and what you need from the model.

values.label: A style, format or smaller model

small.why: Under about 200,000 tokens Anthropic says the knowledge base can go straight into the prompt.

large.why: Window limits, context rot and the 272K price step on GPT-6.

static.why: A stable prompt is easy to keep.

perdoc.why: Everything in the prompt is visible to every caller, so you cannot filter per user.

facts.why: The model reads the source text directly.

behavior.why: Few-shot examples steer style but cost tokens on every call.

small.why: Works, but may be more machinery than needed.

live.why: Re-index changed documents with no retraining.

perdoc.why: Per-user filters and citations are native strengths.

facts.why: RAG consistently beat unsupervised fine-tuning for knowledge.

behavior.why: Retrieval does not change style or format.

small.why: The paper says it suits a limited, manageable knowledge base.

large.why: The corpus must fit the window.

static.why: The cache pays off when content is stable.

live.why: A changed corpus invalidates the cached state.

one.why: One shared cached context for one audience.

perdoc.why: A shared cached context cannot be filtered per user.

facts.why: No retrieval step, so no retrieval misses.

small.why: Little data to learn from, and the prompt can hold it.

large.why: Evidence says RAG beats fine-tuning for facts at any size.

live.why: Facts go stale and retraining is slow.

perdoc.why: Whatever is trained in is visible to every caller.

facts.why: New facts are learned slowly and then raise hallucination.

behavior.why: Format, tone, smaller models and tool-use behaviour are what tuning is for.

blocks.takeaway: Facts belong in retrieval or the prompt. Behaviour belongs in tuning. Per-user permissions rule out any approach that puts the whole corpus into one shared context.

blocks.caption: Fine-tuning methods (checked 2026-10-13)
head: Method
Use it when
Facts to know
rows: You can show the right answer.
OpenAI: minimum 10 examples, gains often at 50 to 100, listed models are the `gpt-4.1` family [[r52]].
You have preferred and rejected pairs.
OpenAI: `beta` between 0 and 2, `gpt-4.1` family, added 2025-06-04 [[r53]]. DPO replaces the RLHF reward model and RL loop with a classification loss [[r46]].
You can write a reliable grader.
OpenAI: `o4-mini` only, launched 2025-05-07 [[r54]]. Azure: `o4-mini`, and `gpt-5` by invitation only [[r17]].

LoRA freezes weights and trains low-rank matrices: 10,000x fewer trainable parameters and 3x less GPU memory than full Adam fine-tuning of GPT-3 175B, with no added inference latency [[r45]]. QLoRA tunes a 65B model on one 48GB GPU [[r25]].
You want a small model to copy a large one.
Train on the large model's outputs (Hinton et al., 2015) [[r47]]. OpenAI's pattern: tune a prompt on a large model, then fine-tune a smaller model on its outputs.

items.symptom: Answers are right in short tests and wrong deep in a long prompt
items.cause: Accuracy depends on length and position, and drops for facts in the middle [[r40]].
items.fix: Test at your real length, place key facts early or late, and retrieve less instead of pasting more.

items.symptom: Answers go stale after the documents change
items.cause: A cached or pasted corpus, or facts trained into weights, no longer matches the source.
items.fix: Use RAG with re-indexing, or rebuild the cache on every change.

items.symptom: A fine-tuned model states wrong facts with confidence
items.cause: Training on new facts raises hallucination once the facts are learned [[r44]].
items.fix: Move facts to retrieval and tune for format and behaviour only.

items.symptom: A user sees content they should not
items.cause: The whole corpus sits in one shared prompt, cache or set of weights.
items.fix: Filter per user with retrieval and ACLs (see w07), or separate contexts per tenant.

items.symptom: A planned OpenAI fine-tuning project cannot start
items.cause: OpenAI is winding down self-serve fine-tuning. Orgs that never ran it could not create jobs from 2026-05-07 [[r11]].
items.fix: Check eligibility first. Consider Azure managed fine-tuning or LoRA on open weights.

items.title: Go deeper: fine-tuning platform status on 2026-10-13

items: OpenAI notice 2026-05-07. From that date orgs that never ran fine-tuning cannot create jobs. From 2026-07-02 orgs with no fine-tuned inference in 60 days cannot. On 2027-01-06 active customers can no longer create jobs. Fine-tuned inference ends only when the base model is deprecated, and several `ft-` models end 2026-10-23 [[r11]].
The GPT-6 Astra page marks the fine-tuning endpoint unsupported [[r1]].

Azure keeps managed SFT, DPO and RFT. Interactive training is Preview and needs approval. Training types are Standard, Data zone (US only), Global and Developer (preemptible, no SLA). Managed compute with LoRA adapters is Preview. Training on the `gpt-4.1` family ends no earlier than 2027-04-14 for existing customers [[r17]].

items.title: Go deeper: why CAG still needs prompt caching

blocks.md: CAG is the idea. Prompt caching is one way to pay for it. Provider caches expire and key on exact prefixes, so a stable ordering and a refresh plan matter. World 2 covers cache keys, time to live and what breaks hit rates. Study material on tuning: [[r27]]. On tokenizers: [[r28]]. Azure path: [[r26]].

quiz.q: A cache-augmented setup serves a 150,000-token manual to one audience. Then documents become visible per user and updates arrive daily. What does the board flip to?
options: A larger context window with the same cache
RAG with per-user filters and re-indexing
The same setup with a shorter cache lifetime
quiz.explain: A shared cached context cannot be filtered per user, and daily updates invalidate it. RAG filters per user and re-indexes changes. A bigger window or shorter lifetime keeps the shared context, and fine-tuning is weak for current facts and exposes trained content to everyone.

quiz.q: A 200,000-token prompt is sent 1,000 times a day to `gpt-6-sol` at $2 per 1M input tokens, with no caching (below the 272K step). A RAG pipeline would send 6,000 input tokens per query instead. How many more dollars per day does the long prompt cost in input tokens?
quiz.hint: Compute each side in millions of tokens, then subtract.
quiz.explain: Long prompt: 200,000 x 1,000 = 200M tokens x $2 = $400. RAG: 6,000 x 1,000 = 6M tokens x $2 = $12. The difference is $388. Prompt caching changes this: reads at $0.2 per 1M would put the long prompt near $40 if every call hit the cache, which is why CAG can compete for small stable corpora.

quiz.q: Select the evidence-backed reasons not to fine-tune a model in order to add facts.
options: RAG beat unsupervised fine-tuning for old and new knowledge
Models learn new facts slowly and then hallucinate more
Azure says fine-tuning does not replace retrieval for current information
quiz.explain: Ovadia et al., Gekhman et al. and Azure's guidance all point away from fine-tuning for facts. LoRA adds no inference latency, and fine-tuned models can call tools, with strict mode lost only for fine-tuned models that make several calls in one turn.

takeaways: Long inputs degrade with length and position, so a big window is not a big usable window
Facts belong in the prompt or retrieval, behaviour belongs in tuning
Per-user permissions rule out shared contexts, caches and trained-in knowledge
OpenAI self-serve fine-tuning is winding down, so check platform eligibility before you plan on it
